query: What visit-note signals suggest high urgency?

per_column.name: signal_critical_vitals
per_column.rationale: Presence of critical vital signs in the note is a clinical variable distinct from the urgency label and plausibly predictive of it; not a restatement or deterministic function of the recorded urgency.

per_column.name: signal_acute_symptoms
per_column.rationale: Acute symptom mentions are note-derived features external to the urgency variable that carry genuine predictive signal about urgency.

per_column.name: signal_acute_onset
per_column.rationale: Acute onset extracted from the note is an independent clinical descriptor plausibly correlated with urgency, not a restatement of it.

per_column.name: signal_high_risk_dx
per_column.rationale: High-risk diagnosis flag is an outside variable with legitimate predictive relevance to urgency; it describes clinical content rather than the urgency label itself.

per_column.name: signal_severe_pain
per_column.rationale: Severe pain is a note signal external to urgency; though observed constant (all 0) here, semantically it is a valid predictor, only weak due to zero variance in this sample.

per_column.name: urgency_signal_count
per_column.rationale: This is a deterministic aggregation (sum) of the individual signal_* columns. As a composite of the same features it adds no independent information beyond them and is a mechanical roll-up rather than a new outside predictor.

per_column.name: urgency_signal_tier
per_column.rationale: A binned/thresholded version of urgency_signal_count, hence a deterministic function of the other columns; it re-expresses the same signal aggregation and contributes no new predictive leverage. Its 'urgency' naming also risks conflation with the focus label.

judge.rationale: Five of the added columns are genuine note-derived clinical signals (critical vitals, acute symptoms, acute onset, high-risk diagnosis, severe pain) that lie outside the urgency label and plausibly predict it, giving real predictive leverage beyond the original columns. The remaining two (count and tier) are deterministic aggregations/binnings of those signals and add no independent information. Predictive utility is moderate rather than high because several signals are extremely sparse (near-constant, one all-zero), limiting realized discriminative power in this sample.
